content.comment_body: Hello, I am wondering if there is a difference when a counter is connected directly to a high-speed input compared to placing the counter inside a User Defined Function (UDF) with a 'direct' connection. I appreciate any insights. This question was separated from a previous thread on high-speed inputs.

Please open a separate topic for new questions in the future. Regarding your query, if the counter is placed inside a UDF, the maximum counting frequency may no longer reach 5 kHz. This is because the UDF executes cyclically and the achievable counting frequency depends on the cycle time, unlike a counter directly associated with the high-speed input.

analysis.insight_summary: A user seeks clarification on whether the placement of a counter inside a UDF, as opposed to directly connecting it to a high-speed input, affects the maximum counting frequency. The response explains that using a UDF makes the counting frequency dependent on the UDF's execution cycle, which may limit performance compared to a direct connection.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates that a counter within a UDF will perform at the same speed as when connected directly to a high-speed input, or seeks to understand any possible differences in performance.
gain_keywords: clear behavior of UDF vs direct input
pain_keywords: potential loss of high speed counting
